headline: Integrating omics and network data with machine learning for cancer prediction
label: Multi Omics Integration Methods
summary: Multi-layer molecular integration is being applied to outcome prediction, subtype classification, and cross-modal inference, where single data layers fall…
synthesis: The dominant thread is integrating heterogeneous molecular data, including transcriptomic and multi-omics profiles, histopathology images, gene-disease associations and metabolite-protein networks, to infer outcomes, subtypes and associations that single data layers do not resolve. MOTLAB applies weighted multi-omics transfer learning with data augmentation to breast cancer outcome prediction in Black women using TCGA data, and MetaPaCS stacks 10 base classifiers on transcriptomic features for pancreatic cancer subtypes. DriverSub-SVM fuses patient-specific and cohort-wide driver gene rankings through random walks, BPR and Condorcet aggregation, while PathGen generates gene expression from histopathology whole-slide images to improve multimodal grading and survival prediction. What is new is explicit attention to how the joint representation is constructed: generated cross-modal features, weighted transfer, and aggregated driver rankings. Reported results derive from different datasets and endpoints and are not directly comparable.
